routing.tribal_contact_limit: Regional starting contacts, not an exhaustive affected-tribe list or a finding that every Tribe must approve. Ask the lead agency and Tribes to identify all affected governments, including interests outside reservation boundaries.

region.critical_area_note: KCC 21A.24 regulates critical areas, buffers and setbacks even where an inventory map has no feature. The County reports updated rules effective February 18, 2026 outside shoreline jurisdiction. Existing critical-area determinations, application completeness and shoreline rules can change vesting. Confirm the applicable revision before using a prior report or assuming a buffer.

wa-king-county-source.jurisdiction: Unincorporated King permit fees and review
wa-king-county-source.citation: Unincorporated King permit fees and review
wa-king-county-source.excerpt: The residential schedule separates application review, site review, inspection and conditional sprinkler review; complex site work can incur additional charges.

wa-king-seattle-source.excerpt: The development fee index determines building and plan review charges; land-use review and site-specific services are separate fees.

wa-king-redmond-source.excerpt: Residential fees combine valuation-based building review, planning, transportation and fire review with a technology surcharge and state fee.

wa-king-sammamish-source.excerpt: Building and planning review carry a technology surcharge; land development, critical-area review and impact charges are separate components.

wa-king-kent-source.excerpt: The building permit schedule uses project valuation; separate planning, engineering, plan-check and impact charges must also be scoped.

wa-king-kent-planning.excerpt: Critical-area report review and mitigation review are separate planning fees, with different schedules for residential and other development.

wa-king-bellevue-source.excerpt: Adopted ordinance separates building inspection, plan review, residential planning review and trade inspection charges; new dwellings receive a construction-review adjustment.

wa-king-renton-source.excerpt: The published city schedule separates building review, site/zoning and engineering review, combination trade permits, and the technology surcharge.

wa-king-kirkland-source.excerpt: The city publishes its own development fee schedule; municipal building, land-use and engineering charges require city-specific pricing.

wa-king-water.excerpt: A well permit exemption does not establish legal water availability; confirm watershed restrictions and an adequate potable supply before committing to development.

wa-king-consultants.citation: Environmental consulting hourly rate and service counties
wa-king-consultants.excerpt: This consultant publishes an hourly environmental-services rate and expressly serves both King and Skagit counties; project hours require a separate scope.

wa-king-tribal-contacts.excerpt: The state publishes tribal-government contacts for consultation; affected tribes must be identified for the particular location, resources and proposed activity.

wa-king-septic-fees.citation: King public health septic fee schedule
wa-king-septic-fees.excerpt: The published schedule identifies separate review charges for this service; applicability and additional work depend on the project scope.

wa-king-screening.excerpt: Applications requiring plan review and completeness screening carry a separate screening charge. The 2026 provision expires at the start of the next calendar year.

wa-king-seattle-landuse.label: Seattle: conditional MUP / land-use review allowance
wa-king-seattle-landuse.note: SMC 22.900B.010 and Table C-1: $551/hour; general MUP review minimum covers 10 hours. This editable 10–30-hour bidding allowance is an assumed review scope, not an agency quote or maximum. Only applies if this type of land-use review is required; routine code-compliant homes may not need a MUP. Intake, notice, specialized exceptions and other charges are additional; confirm category and hours with SDCI.
